{"verdict":"ANSWER","answer":"Experiment: keep 8 processes but raise arenas per process from 40 to 80 (8p80), holding the 8320/1680 GPU/CPU split and everything else fixed.

Why it's new: you tested 4p80 (worse, 17.8s) and 16p40 (worse, 34s), but never doubled arenas while keeping process count. 8p40 runs 208 sequential batches; each batch is a commit + waitUntilCompleted, so the GPU drains fully between batches and the post-prefetch dependent slices (latency-bound random 1KiB reference reads in slices 2-3) run at only 320 concurrent warps. 8p80 doubles in-flight shards to 640, doubling memory-level parallelism exactly where the kernel is latency-limited, and halves per-batch commit/setup/blit overhead. No parameter, root, or count change: workers is purely a batching knob (read from header, MAX_WORKERS=256 allows 80).

Exact code point: invocation only - set workers=80 in the header consumed at brainvault_argon2_metal.m main; buffer sizing (bytes_per_shard*workers) and the device.maxBufferLength guard (~line 168) already handle 20GiB/process; the batch loop (~line 196) and dispatch math are workers-agnostic. Zero code edits.

Risk: 4p80's regression hints arena count may interact with CPU-side balance, so keep the CPU shard assignment identical to the 14.26s run; watch for allocation failure (guarded) and memory pressure (8x20GiB=160GiB, fine on 512GiB). Measure with BRAINVAULT_METAL_PROFILE: if GPU command time doesn't drop below ~11.6s, the bottleneck is the serial dependency chain, not concurrency - stop.
